alternate_names: Sri Nettikanti Anjaneya Swamy Vari Temple

history.period: 1509-1530 CE (prathista by Sri Vyasaraja; Vyasaraya attained mukti in 1539 CE)
history.summary: The Kasapuram Nettikanti Anjaneya Swamy Temple is a renowned Hanuman shrine in Kasapuram village, Guntakal Mandal, Anantapur district, Andhra Pradesh. During the reign of Vijayanagara emperor Sri Krishnadevaraya, his guru Sri Vyasarayaluvaru (Vyasaraja), while travelling from his stay at Silpagiri (Chippagiri, Kurnool district), had a dream in which Hanuman directed him to reinstall an idol at the spot where a withered margosa (neem) tree would revive when he touched it. At Nettikallu he found the withered tree turn green, unearthed a 10-foot idol, and consecrated it as Nettikanti Anjaneya Swamy - 'nettikanti' referring to the deity gracing devotees with his right eye. The temple was built in 1509-1530 CE; Vyasaraya is credited with installing 732 Hanuman idols across the kingdom and attained mukti in 1539 CE. The east-facing temple has a 70-foot five-tier rajagopuram with gold-plated kalasas, a wooden mukha-dwaram covered with engraved silver plates, and Dravidian architecture. Poojas follow the Pancharatra Agama; thousands of pilgrims visit on Saturdays and it is believed devotees suffering from uncured ailments receive cures. CORRECTION: the CSV lists town as 'Anantapur' - that is the district; the temple is in Kasapuram village, Guntakal Mandal. name: Kasapuram Nettikanti Anjaneya Swamy Temple
town_description: Kasapuram is a village in Guntakal Mandal, Anantapur district, Andhra Pradesh, a short drive from Guntakal town. It is best known for the Nettikanti Anjaneya Swamy Temple, which draws thousands of devotees, especially on Saturdays.
tradition: Vaishnavism (Hanuman worship; poojas per Pancharatra Agama)

travel.airport: Bengaluru International Airport, about 250 km away (per Velpu).
travel.railway: Guntakal Railway Junction - distance conflicting across sources: 3.5 km per Velpu, about 11 km per prayanamam.com. Verify locally.
travel.road: About 9 km from the Guntakal bus terminal (per prayanamam.com); direct buses run to the temple.
